subject: Per-token threshold reconciliation and marginal math for ACME pilot
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Per-token threshold reconciliation and marginal math for ACME pilot

Hi Elena / ACME procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — quick follow up with two clean ways we typically structure per-token discounts for hosted API commits. Attached is a modeled workbook (ACME_pricing_model_v1.xlsx) with the numbers below so you can play with the ramp.

High-level options (for 150M tokens/mo commit baseline):
- Marginal ladder (classic breakpoints):
  - 0-49,999,999 tokens: $0.00080 / token
  - 50,000,000-99,999,999 tokens: $0.00060 / token
  - 100,000,000+: $0.00045 / token
  - Effective (if you hit 150M): weighted marginal effective ~ $0.00055 / token

- Blended slab (single effective rate by tier):
  - 0-149,999,999 (committed band): $0.00058 / token (one invoiceable effective rate)
  - Overusage billed at list $0.00080 unless we apply pre-agreed overage credits

Why it matters: marginal gives the lowest marginal cost at high consumption but complicates forecasting and invoice reconciliation. Blended is simpler for finance teams who want a single line item and predictable effective cost, at the expense of slightly higher headroom for Redwood.

Two questions so we can pick the right structure for ACME:
1) Do you prefer a simple blended effective rate for predictability or a marginal ladder to capture upside?
2) Are you comfortable with a monthly true-up (standard) or would you prefer a quarterly true-up with a monthly cap on overage invoices?

If you prefer, I can propose a hybrid: a blended committed rate for the baseline with marginal burst credits (e.g., up to 30% over baseline: marginal pricing applied as a credit). That preserves predictability and gives ACME burst efficiency.

Attached: ACME_pricing_model_v1.xlsx (breakpoint math + blended examples)

Next step: if you can tell me which direction (blended vs marginal vs hybrid) and expected ramp months 1-3, I’ll send a formal proposal with line items and sample invoices.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Per-token threshold reconciliation and marginal math for ACME pilot

Ben / Soojin — forwarding Elena's note. She wants blended for GL simplicity with a capped overage. My proposed mechanics:

Proposal idea (internal):
- Committed band: blended effective rate for the committed volume (month-by-month) — single invoice line.
- Overage treatment: define a capped overage policy where any consumption over committed band up to +30% is billed at a pre-agreed preferential overage rate (e.g., $0.00060), and true spikes above committed+30% billed at list $0.00080.
- True-up cadence: monthly accounting true-up, but finance wants to see a sample table; if they require quarterly true-up, we can convert but need to push some crediting logic into contract.

Quick numeric example for month 3 (expected 150M actual, committed 150M):
- If committed = 150M and actual = 150M => invoice = 150M * blended_committed_rate.
- If committed = 150M and actual = 180M (+20%): invoice = 150M * blended_committed_rate + 30M * preferential_overage_rate.
- If actual = 220M (+46%): invoice = 150M * blended_committed_rate + 45M * preferential_overage_rate (capped at 30%) + 25M * list_rate.

I recommend offering a hybrid: blended committed rate = $0.00057, preferential overage = $0.00060 (applies up to +30%), list = $0.00080. This gets them predictability and gives them efficient burst economics. Our margin remains reasonable and ops billing is one-line for committed.

Action: Ben — can you sanity-check the margin at blended $0.00057 vs our kernel-level cost assumptions? Soojin — can you draft a short statement we can add to the SOW about the capped overage mechanics and true-up cadence (monthly by default, quarterly on request)?

Thanks,
Jonas

Subject: Final pricing summary: blended baseline + capped overage (sample invoice table)

Elena — thanks for the quick feedback and the commit profile. Per our internal check we landed on a conservative hybrid that matches your finance preference for a single-line committed invoice while protecting both sides from runaway usage. Attached is a short PDF with a sample invoice table (20261209-ACME-pricing-summary.pdf). Key points below: 

Final proposal (pilot / first 6 months):
- Committed baseline: 150,000,000 tokens / month (3-month ramp: 50M -> 100M -> 150M)
- Blended committed rate: $0.00057 / token (single invoice line for committed consumption)
- Preferential overage: up to +30% over committed volume billed at $0.00060 / token (applies to the portion up to +30%)
- List overage: consumption above committed +30% billed at list $0.00080 / token
- True-up cadence: monthly by default; option for quarterly invoicing with quarterly true-up and capped monthly overage invoices (contractual appendix)
- Sample invoice month 3 (actual 180M):
  - Committed: 150M * $0.00057 = $85,500
  - Overage (30M) * $0.00060 = $18,000
  - Total = $103,500

Rationale: blended committed makes your GL team happy, preferential overage preserves burst economics, and the capped overage prevents surprise large bills. If you want the marginal ladder instead we can show a second tab in the workbook with marginal breakpoints and the exact blended-equivalent so your FP&A can compare side-by-side.

Next steps:
1) If this looks good I’ll work with Legal to add the overage appendix and send a redline-friendly SOW.
2) Please confirm whether you want monthly or quarterly true-up (if quarterly, we’ll propose the appendix language).
3) If you’d like a 30-minute call I can run FP&A through the sample invoice table next week. HubSpot link to the deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ACME-2026-01
